answer: One check that is hard for a sybil farm to dodge is a perturbation probe. Each epoch the network quietly varies a small kernel of the prompt for a random subset of accounts, then watches how the change spreads. Independent agents react in scattered, unrelated ways; accounts run by one operator tend to shift together, a ripple that shows up across the whole cluster within the same window. Rewards for correlated accounts stay locked past the vesting horizon until the pattern clears, so a farm pays for every copy it runs.
